subject: Mid-quarter check: QBR prep, scope updates & cross-team dependency asks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-quarter check: QBR prep, scope updates & cross-team dependency asks

Team / Sarah —

Quick mid-quarter note ahead of next week’s QBR prep week. High-level status against the product reliability & partner expansion OKRs we committed to:

- Reliability/latency: avg p95 for hosted API is 230ms; KV-cache work reduced tails but we still see spikes on long-seq workloads.
- Partner integrations: Acme integration proof-of-concept is functionally stable; need security checklist closure and end-to-end perf numbers.
- Cost optimization: Explore batching profiles for chat flows — runway looks OK but needs a small infra allocation to test.

Asks (priority ordered):
1) Vanessa: can we make a short-term Dedicated capacity reservation (2 GPUs) for the integration smoke window (target: Aug 16–30)? Budget check please.
2) Neha: can Security prioritize the Acme questionnaire answers (SOC scope + data flow diagram) by Aug 11? Sarah, can you confirm what you need from us?
3) Karthik: can you confirm whether we can run the new batching profile experiment without impacting the staging cluster SLA? If not, propose a narrower run.

Attached is a draft QBR slide deck (QBR-slides-draft.pdf) and I’ve added a skeleton mutual action plan in Confluence (link below). I’ll consolidate commits into a final MAP by Aug 12.

Goal for this thread: lock down who owns what by EOD Friday so we can bake into the QBR narrative.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Head of Product, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-quarter check: QBR prep, scope updates & cross-team dependency asks

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear note. Acme is onboard to help drive E2E perf validation; a couple quick asks from our side:
- We need the API contract + sample payloads by Aug 10 to schedule our integration engineers.
- We will run an internal security scan; please send the minimal scoping answers for the SOC-style checklist (data types, retention, encryption in transit/at rest).

On Dedicated capacity: we can align our smoke window to whatever you can provision; if you target Aug 16–30, our team can put folks on standby.

One ask: can Redwood provide a simple telemetry stream (tokenized event counts + latency buckets) for the smoke window so we can compare against our baseline? If that’s not feasible, a shared set of synthetic traces will work.

Happy to jump on a 30-min alignment call if helpful — my availability Tues/Thurs morning next week.

—Sarah
Sarah Liu | Dir, Integrations — Acme Corp
sarah.liu@acme.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-quarter check: QBR prep, scope updates & cross-team dependency asks

Marissa / team —

Quick technical readout: the new batching profile reduces token cost ~14% in ideal cases but increases p95 by ~40–60ms under bursty arrival patterns due to longer accumulation windows. We can run the experiment on staging without SLA impact if we narrow the test to:
- single model variant (bert-qa-1)
- capped concurrency (<= 80 concurrent requests)
- synthetic replay of 48 hours of traffic across 2 replicas

If we need production-closest numbers for Acme, we’ll require a short Dedicated reservation (as called out) and a rollback plan.

I attached a quick csv with simulated latency deltas (latency-impact-analysis.csv). My recommendation to keep QBR messaging tight: we describe the batching experiment as "cost/latency tradeoff evaluation" and commit to decision by Aug 25. If leadership wants a shorter decision timeline, we should de-scope the A/B to a single subset of traffic.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Mid-quarter check: QBR prep, scope updates & cross-team dependency asks

Thanks for the clear asks. I’ll commit the following for the QBR window (pending a short budget note):
- Reassign one SWE (2 sprints) to own the Acme smoke plan and final MAP updates.
- Approve a temporary Dedicated reservation equivalent to 2 x A100s for Aug 16–30. Finance to sign off on Monday; assume verbal approval for planning.

Neha — please prioritize the questionnaire responses; if you need exceptions for unusual data flows, escalate to me directly.

Marissa — please update the mutual action plan in Confluence with the owners and timelines so Finance and Legal can see the commitments. If we need to tighten scope to meet the approval cycle, I support the narrower A/B recommendation Karthik suggested.

Vanessa Ortiz | VP, Product Operations, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — summary and next steps (owners / deadlines):

1) Dedicated capacity (2 x A100s): Vanessa -> tentative approval; Finance will confirm Mon Aug 10. Action: Vanessa to confirm by EOD Mon; Marissa to queue provisioning request on Aug 11.
2) Security questionnaire: Neha -> deliver answers + minimal data flow diagram by Aug 11. Action: Neha owns; Sarah to review and confirm sufficiency.
3) Batching experiment scope: Karthik -> run capped-staging run and produce results by Aug 20. If staging numbers look promising, we run the smoke on Dedicated Aug 16–20.
4) MAP & QBR slides: Marissa -> update Confluence MAP and slide deck with owners and timelines by Aug 12 (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cQBR-draft).

If anyone disagrees with the timeline or ownership, flag now — otherwise I’ll bake this into the QBR narrative and the plan for the exec readout.

Appreciate the quick alignment.

—Marissa
